name: Irena Arslanova
title: Dr.
headline: Why do some moments fly by while others seem to stretch endlessly?
bio: As a Leverhulme Early-Career Fellow at Royal Holloway, University of London's Psychology Department, I investigate the mysteries of time perception: why some moments fly by while others seem to stretch endlessly. My research explores how our internal bodily rhythms, particularly heartbeats, distort our experience of time.

During my PhD at University College London, I studied how scattered touch sensations coalesce into unified perceptions rather than remaining fragmented impressions. My work also examines attention, emotion, and embodiment, revealing how we activate our own internal body maps when trying to understand others.
